summary: Faster on a Mac and on a Steam Deck, the first-start picture bug fixed, and Lichii nx2 of late November.

changes.title: Faster on a Mac
changes.body: The bundled MoltenVK lets Metal optimize the shaders' precise arithmetic, and more of the game's compute work takes the fast path. On an Apple M6, Ocarina of Time goes from about 37 frames per second to the game's 60 standing still, and from 34 to 52 turning the camera.

changes.title: First-start picture bug fixed
changes.body: On macOS the picture could come out white, dark or covered in stretched triangles on a first start with nothing built yet. That is fixed.

changes.title: A core for the GPU thread on four-core CPUs
changes.body: On Linux, on CPUs with four cores and eight threads such as the Steam Deck's, the GPU thread gets a core to itself. On a Steam Deck, Ocarina of Time gains 3 to 6 % with default power settings, and up to 12 % with the GPU clock fixed at 1600 MHz and GameMode turned off in the emulator's settings. GameMode undoes the thread layout unless its CPU pinning is turned off; the log explains how.

changes.title: Optimization profiles that apply in full
changes.body: The PGO builds for Linux and Windows are trained on this build's code, and no longer lose part of the profile because of the folder they were built in.

changes.title: From Lichii nx2
changes.body: Fixes for textures used after they were retired, shader translation fixes, saves and installs that failed on open files on Windows, an option to keep the window size, and fixes for several other titles.

changes.title: About this build
changes.body: This is a build of the zelda branch of danieljesus/Lichii, not an official Lichii release. Reopen these notes anytime from Help, even offline.
